The Rays acquired Peralta from the Mets at the trade deadline and his turnaround has propelled them to the World Series

        The Tampa Bay Rays are going to the World Series for the third time in franchise history and trade deadline pickup Freddy Peralta is a big reason why. Peralta was named ALCS MVP after holding the Cleveland Guardians to one run in 5 ⅓ innings in Monday's Game 6 win. He allowed just the one run in 12 innings across two starts and one relief appearances in the ALCS.
"Milwaukee is the team and the city that gave me the opportunity to make my dream," Peralta said about facing the Milwaukee Brewers, his former team, in the World Series.Peralta threw six shutout innings in Tampa's Game 2 win, though his biggest outing of the ALCS might have been his Game 4 relief appearance. He entered with the tying run on base and the go-ahead run at the plate in the sixth inning, then retired Steven Kwan and Chase DeLauter to preserve a one-run lead in an eventual win. Peralta appeared in three of Tampa's four ALCS wins.
Acquired from the New York Mets at the trade deadline, Peralta has pitched to a 2.75 ERA in 72 innings with the Rays between the regular season and postseason. He threw 113 ⅔ innings with a 4.99 ERA for New York. The Rays had Peralta pitch from the stretch, throw more changeups, and raise his arm angle. That led to his increased success after the trade.The 30-year-old Peralta will be a free agent after the season and his performance with the Rays has boosted his stock, certainly. First things first, though. Peralta is the ALCS MVP and now he will try to help the Rays beat his former team in the World Series.
Neither the Brewers nor Rays have ever won the World Series. We're guaranteed a first-time champion in 2026.

title: 'I need the ball': Inside what fueled Angel Reese to one of the best performances in WNBA Finals history - CBS Sports
description: Reese demanded the ball and supplied the Dream with 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 against the Valkyries
body:
Reese demanded the ball and supplied the Dream with 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 against the Valkyries

        SAN FRANCISCO -- Ninety minutes before tip-off on Monday, Angel Reese finished her pre-game warm-up and walked straight to a scrum of a dozen media members waiting in a tunnel. The youngest member of the Atlanta Dream's starting five made no excuses for how Game 1 ended. She only promised that Game 2 would be better. "I can't let my team down," Reese said. In front of another hostile Ballhalla crowd that booed her introduction louder than any other Atlanta player, and erupted every time she was called for a foul, Reese carried the Dream to a 79-65 win over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 2 of the 2026 WNBA Finals. She finished with a playoff-career-high 30 points on 10 of 16 from the field, 16 rebounds, three assists, a steal and two blocks in 34 minutes. The best performance of her young career not only evened the Finals at 1-1, but gave the Dream their first Finals victory in franchise history. "That's what we expect from her night in, night out. She's young and she hasn't been here before, but that's not an excuse," DeWanna Bonner told CBS Sports after Reese became the third player in WNBA history with 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals game. "We ride her back, we ride her coattail, we ride her energy. We expect that from her every single game."
Dream coach Karl Smesko had a feeling Game 2 would go his team's way when he walked into the locker room before tip-off and made eye contact with Reese. "I was like, 'Oh, I like that look," Smesko said. Reese's teammates saw it too. "You can just see that she wants it really bad. She's such a competitor and we feed off of her energy," Jordin Canada said. "She set the tone for sure, and it trickled down to the whole team."
Reese, who didn't score in the second half of Game 1 and took only three shots in the final 26 minutes, pledged to be more "assertive" on Monday. She followed through immediately. Forty seconds in, she had to reach back and make a catch with one hand because she was trying to drive before she even had the ball. Once she had possession, she blew past Cecilia Zandalasini for a layup. Reese ran in transition. She rolled and drove to the basket, going around or through whatever defender the Valkyries threw in her path. By halftime, she was up to 15 points, and the Dream had a two-point lead. 
But early in the third, it seemed Reese and the Dream might be in for a repeat of Game 1. Kiah Stokes demolished Reese's first shot attempt of the second half and she went nearly four minutes without getting another look. In the middle of the frame, Reese got so frustrated that she threw her arms up in dismay in the middle of a possession and screamed at the bench. At one point she was like, 'I need the ball, I need the ball,'" Canada said. "We gave her the ball, and she went to work."The very next time down the floor, Reese took a hit-ahead pass from Allisha Gray, surged down the lane for an and-one and let out a roar as she celebrated with her teammates. The three-point play broke a tie and was the start of an 18-4 run to close the third that put the Dream up by 14 and the game out of reach. Reese had nine of the 18 points. "I wanted to make sure I came out tonight and left my mark and did whatever I could to get the win, and I think I did that," Reese said.
What Smesko called a "superior performance" from Reese was the latest in an incredible first playoff run for the third-year forward. The Dream acquired Reese in the offseason from the Chicago Sky because they thought her "drive to win," in addition to her talent, could put them over the top after three consecutive first-round exits. No matter what happens in the rest of this series, Dan Padover and Co. have already been proven correct. Allisha Gray missed all but 11 minutes of the semifinals with a hand injury and Rhyne Howard is shooting 22 of 82 (26.8%) over her last five games, but Reese has picked up the slack. She's in double figures in all seven playoff games and is averaging 19.1 points, 10 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.6 steals and two blocks on 46.8% shooting, while being the team's emotional leader. And Reese has done it despite facing what Bonner called "a different type of pressure." 
"The women's game has changed and she's part of the reason why it has. People expect a lot of things out of Angel," Bonner said. "She focuses on what Angel can control and what Angel can do. She accepts the challenges that she gets from her coaches and teammates, and she just performs."Far from letting her team down, Reese's latest performance has the Dream three wins away from the first title in franchise history.

        Injuries keep piling up for the San Francisco 49ers as star wide receiver Mike Evans left Monday night's game late in the first half with an Achilles injury and was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Evans was listed as questionable heading into the primetime contest against the Commanders, but managed to play and caught 3 passes for 94 yards before leaving. He was grabbing his Achilles after making a catch.Head coach Kyle Shanahan noted this week that Evans was dealing with Achilles soreness. The wideout did not practice at all this week, which left his status for Week 6 firmly up in the air for a big NFC matchup.Evans did not practice at all this week, with reports noting that he was mostly working off to the side. 
The 33-year-old has a history of playing through injuries and has not missed a contest to this point despite missing time in practice. Last week, Evans missed Thursday's practice with his rib injury, but ended up playing in the Week 5 win over Seattle. That said, this is the first time all season that Evans missed the entire week of practice. Evans signed a three-year, $42.4 million deal with the 49ers at the start of free agency, snapping his 12-season tenure with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. So far, the future Hall of Fame receiver has been as advertised and is coming off his first 100-yard game of the season, hauling in seven balls for 113 yards and a touchdown in the win over the Seahawks. Through five games, Evans has caught 24 of his 34 targets for 326 yards and three touchdowns. 
The 49ers offense was already without fellow receivers Deebo Samuel Jr., who was ruled out with a hamstring injury, and Christian Kirk with a calf injury.

Next season is the final season on Boone's contract and will be his 10th season as Yankees manager. New York is 790-565 (.583) in nine seasons under Boone. The Yankees have reached the postseason eight times in those nine seasons but have not won the World Series."That's for another day," Boone said when asked about his job status after the Yankees were swept by the AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. "Right now is about trying to reflect on this, trying to connect with guys right now as much as I can.  Appreciative of a lot of things, but those conversations and things are for another day."Unless the Yankees give Boone a contract extension, he will enter next season as a lame duck, and that season could come with a World Series or bust mandate. The Yankees have had only three managers in the last 30 years: Joe Torre from 1996-2007, Joe Girardi from 2008-17, and Boone since 2018. Torre and Girardi both won the World Series within their first two seasons.Why the Yankees are sticking with BooneThe Yankees have not fired a manager who was under contract since Stump Merrill after the 1991 season (Torre and Girardi were let go after their contracts expired). Hal Steinbrenner is much more patient than his father, perhaps to his detriment, but Steinbrenner and GM Brian Cashman are supportive of Boone. That all made Boone's return more likely than not.
Furthermore, this is a bad offseason to need a new manager. Team personnel, including managers, can not communicate with players during a lockout, which is considered likely when the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1. Relationship-building with players is most of the job, and it will be difficult for a new manager to foster those during the lockout.Only the Los Angeles Dodgers have won more games than the Yankees since Boone was named manager in 2018. This is a franchise that is judged on championships, however, and New York has not won a World Series since 2009. The Yankees have won just one pennant since then (2024), and their 17-year title drought is tied for the longest in franchise history with their 1979-95 stretch.Aaron Boone as Yankees managerSeasonRecordPlayoffs2018100-62Lost ALDS2019103-59Lost ALCS202033-27Lost ALDS202192-70Lost AL Wild Card202299-63Lost ALCS202382-80N/A202494-68Lost World Series202594-68Lost ALDS202693-68Lost ALDSCashman is currently without a contract, though he is expected to return for what would be his 29th season as their head baseball operations executive. Boone's and Cashman's status were two of the biggest questions facing the Yankees this offseason.
The Yankees went 93-68 in 2026. It was their 34th consecutive winning season. The Houston Astros and Seattle Mariners are the only two teams with a managerial vacancy at the moment.

Seriously.After Weeks 5 and 6, this season's NFC East is now the first division in NFL history with consecutive winless weeks with four-plus games played, per CBS Sports Research. The division's four teams are a combined 0-6-2 since Week 5. In Week 5, the Dallas Cowboys (2-4) lost 24-16 at home on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie quarterback, making his second career start. In Week 6, their offense looked lifeless in a 23-13 road loss at the Green Bay Packers on "Sunday Night Football." Dallas also has the NFL's 30th-ranked total defense (382.5 yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (149.8 yards allowed per game), and last-place third-down defense (54.7% third-down conversion rate allowed). The Packers entered Week 6 as the NFL's worst third-down offense with a conversion rate of 27.6%, but they went 11-for-18 on third downs Sunday night. The two-time defending division champion Philadelphia Eagles have the least embarrassing losses of the last two weeks: a 19-17 defeat to the AFC South-leading Jaguars despite kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left, and a 25-14 home defeat to the NFC South-leading Panthers. People faulted coach Nick Sirianni for having the kickoff go in bounds to drain time off the clock in Week 5. The Jaguars returned the kick 53 yards to the Eagles' 39, which set up the game-winning 57-yard field goal for Jacksonville. In Week 6, Philadelphia's Saquon Barkley-less offense wasn't enough to elevate 2023 sixth-round pick quarterback Tanner McKee, even with the return of No. 1 wide receiver DeVonta Smith, in a 25-14 home loss against the NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers. The NFC East-leading New York Giants (3-2-1) tied 27-27 against the last-place Washington Commanders (1-4-1) even though both teams reached field-goal range in the last two minutes of overtime. In Week 6, they trailed by nearly as many as 24 points (34-10) against a New Orleans Saints squad that used the Giants to snap a three-game losing streak in a 34-27 victory. New York is without quarterback Jaxson Dart and All-Pro edge rusher Brian Burns for the year because of season-ending knee injuries. McCarthy, the quarterback who ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (58%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) in 2025. Washington had chances to upset the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers in their 23-17 "Monday Night Football" road loss, but they couldn't finish the job late. 
Somehow, the Cowboys (+130) are the betting favorites to win the NFC East entering Week 7, per DraftKings Sportsbook. The Giants (+154), Commanders (+600) and the Eagles (+700) are how the rest of the odds shake out at this moment in time. Vegas appears out on the Eagles with quarterback Jalen Hurts sidelined by blood clots, but if the last two weeks are any indication, none of the four teams are truly out of the hunt just yet.

title: What's next for Guardians? Biggest offseason questions after ALCS exit - CBS Sports
description: After losing to the Rays in the ALCS, Cleveland is headed home with major questions about several core players
body:
After losing to the Rays in the ALCS, Cleveland is headed home with major questions about several core players
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For the second straight season, the Cleveland Guardians rallied in the second half to win the AL Central, but fell sort of reaching the World Series. Cleveland's season ended when it dropped Game 6 of the best-of-seven ALCS to the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday night (TB 7, CLE 3).The three-time defending AL Central champions now face an important offseason -- they're all important offseasons, but especially this one -- in which several core players are facing a level of uncertainty about their future. Here are three questions facing the Guardians following their ALDS exit.  1. Is José Ramírez still a star? 
This past season, third baseman José Ramírez became the Guardians' franchise leader in games played (1,734) in what turned out to be his worst season since becoming a regular in 2016. He authored a .235/.320/.368 batting line that was down 175 points of OPS and 43 points of OPS+ from last season. Ramírez went from MVP candidate in 2025 to just OK in 2026. Perhaps the hand injury is to blame. Ramírez fractured the hamate bone in his left hand on June 13; at the time, he was hitting .239/.339/.418 through 72 games. That is below his usual production, but isn't bad by any means. After returning from surgery in late July, Ramírez slashed .229/.296/.302 in 53 games with little hard contact. He looked nothing like peak J-Ram. 
 Average exit velocityExpected slugging percentageBefore hamate injury 				90.3 mph 				.444 				After hamate injury 				86.5 mph 				.321 				The Guardians are built offensively around Ramírez, and if he underperforms, the walls begin to cave in. Also, Cleveland signed him to a seven-year, $175 million extension last January. He'll make $25 million a year (roughly 33% of the team's 2026 payroll) through 2032. Ramírez being less than a star will hurt the team on the field and financially. Ramírez turned 34 last month and age-related decline could be coming. Great players age differently than other players, but Father Time is undefeated. For more reasons than one, the Guardians have to hope Ramírez's down 2026 was a result of the hamate injury and not the start of a trend. There simply isn't enough offensive talent to carry the team to a World Series title otherwise.  2. What's the plan with Steven Kwan? 
It was a tale of two seasons for Steven Kwan. Cleveland's longtime leadoff hitter bottomed out at .206/.321/.251 on June 22, making him legitimately one of the worst hitters in baseball. He finished exceptionally well, though, hitting .345/.433/.429 in 80 games after that date. His final batting line -- .282/.382/.349 -- looked like it always does. He just took a bumpy road to get there. Kwan is entering his final season of team control and he's projected for $11 million or so through arbitration, which is a below-market salary but also pricey for the Guardians. His name has popped up in several trade rumors the last 18 months or so, most notably at the 2025 trade deadline. A trade was reportedly close, but Cleveland simply ran out of time before the deadline. The Guardians have three options with Kwan this offseason: Keep him in 2027 and let him become a free agent after the season;Sign him to a long-term extension;Trade him.A long-term extension for a defense-first player with minimal power (a skill that ages well) might not be the best idea for a team with a bottom-of-the-league payroll. Keeping Kwan next year, trying to win with him, then walking him right out onto the open market is a reasonable option. It would just be unfortunate to lose him as a free agent and get nothing in return. At minimum, president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti would not be doing his job if he didn't explore the trade market for Kwan this offseason. You have to at least listen. The one year of control would limit the market to contenders only, but more than a few win-now teams would love to have him. The Chicago Cubs, New York Yankees, Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres all come to mind.The Guardians have traded several of their best and most popular players a year before free agency in recent years (Francisco Lindor, Corey Kluber, etc.) and I do think that is the most likely outcome with Kwan. If the plan was an extension, it would have happened already. Letting him walk in a year for no return is untenable. A trade seems likely. 
 3. Will anyone get an extension? 
Cleveland is the most extension-happy team in the game. They popularized the early career long-term extension strategy under former GM John Hart in the 1990s with Jim Thome, among others. Ramírez and righty Tanner Bibee are currently signed to long-term contracts and it stands to reason the Guardians will look to lock up a few other building blocks soon. They have several worthy extension candidates, too:  CP Cade Smith (free agent after 2028)SP Gavin Williams (free agent after 2029)SP Parker Messick (free agent after 2031)2B Travis Bazzana (free agent after 2032)I'm always nervous about extending pitchers years ahead of free agency because there is so much inherent injury risk, but when you operate with a small payroll like the Guardians, you sometimes have to take that chance. Smith has hefty arbitration salaries coming his way ($6 million or so in 2027) and may want to take things year by year. Cleveland should at least try, though. Extensions are what the Guardians do and I would expect them to explore long-term deals with several players this offseason, particularly those four above. That doesn't mean they'll get agreements done. It takes two to tango and you can't always push these things across the finish line. The Guardians no doubt will try. Those long-term deals are important.

        With nine trophies in their history, the Columbus Crew are among the most successful teams in Major League Soccer, but it has been two years since their last trophy, as much of the team has shifted and wasn't involved in their last trophy, a Leagues Cup win in 2024. Now, as they gear up to host the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup final on Wednesday against St. Louis City SC (live on Paramount+ and CBS Sports Network, 8 p.m. ET), it's a chance to salvage the season, and there are still players there who have experience winning, even in this competition.During the summer, forward Josef Martinez joined the club after what he described as a tough time with Club Tijuana in Liga MX. While at the moment, it was a move that felt like it should be made leaving CF Montreal, sometimes those moves don't work out, but Martinez is also grateful to be with the Crew currently, where he has been able to get back to full fitness and have a chance to contribute now with the chance to win a trophy."We have to recognize that this is an opportunity to turn on the little bit of a struggle season; this is the opportunity to win something," Martinez said. "I have had the opportunity to win one time; I lost one in Miami, and this is my third one. So, it's special when you have a final. I don't remember how many players have the opportunity to play that."Martinez won the Open Cup with Atlanta United in 2018 while also capturing the Golden Boot, MLS Cup, and MVP awards all in that same season. Things haven't gone as expected recently with the Crew being his fifth team in the past three years but that doesn't mean that the 33-year-old Venezuelan doesn't have something to offer the squad both on and off the pitch as they look to secure their first trophy post-Wilfried Nancy. And no matter what, that's a moment worth looking forward to.
"A final is special, man. It's an opportunity to win something with the club. That is the most important right now," Martinez said, summing up the occasion.This isn't something that the Crew will need extra motivation for, as when you're playing a sport that you love, the goal is to get to a moment like this. Martinez may have already etched his name in MLS history, but for many on the team, they'll be looking to him and Mendez to set an example on Wednesday. It's something that Martinez is aware of, and it's a role that he relishes as a veteran of the league. He came to Atlanta to prove that he could make it and became "El Rey" (The king) for a reason, and even at his age, he's still a forward who strikes fear into the opposition, even if they're unbeaten in 22 straight games like St. Louis are."We're professional," Martinez said. "We know what the game is; we know what the situation is right now. And we know that is important. We have to go there and play soccer and fight. That's most important. We play soccer. We don't play any other sport. We have pressure; but they have pressure too. So, I think [who] makes fewer mistakes, they can have the opportunity to win."
Being able to deal with that pressure is something that Martinez brings to this squad, which has undergone plenty of change. The Crew may not make the playoffs as they're 11th in the Eastern Conference, so they'll need to look at this as a moment that will make or break their season. But when looking across the pitch, St. Louis City SC have never been in a final in their history so the pressure will be felt both ways but Martinez's goals can make the difference."Yeah, we're happy [to be in the final], man. When we score, we strikers want to score every game," Martinez said. "And we get frustrated when we can't do, we can't do not that. But it's a game. We have to be ready for all of this. And that will be a tough game because they are a really good team."Martinez will have the squad ready for the task at hand as it's a moment where both he and the Crew can get back to their best while being able to host a final in front of their home fans. You can't ask for a better chance than this in what will be an excellent final.

San Francisco can improve to 6-0 and strengthen its NFC West lead, while Washington enters Levi's Stadium looking to pull off a sizable road upset

        In the Week 6 edition of "Monday Night Football," the San Francisco 49ers play host to the Washington Commanders.San Francisco is riding high atop the NFC West with a 5-0 record, having defeated the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in a barnburner last week. The Niners have battled injuries on both sides of the ball all season, yet have remained unbeaten. They can create a three-game lead in the division with a victory on Monday night.Washington is coming off an absolute debacle last Sunday against the New York Giants, wherein the Commanders had a chance to kick a field goal to win the game at the end of overtime, but bungled the clock management as badly as any team you'll ever see. The Commies are just 1-3-1 entering this game, and they're looking to avoid falling further into the basement in the NFC East.Will the Niners continue to roll, or will the Commanders pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Where to watch 49ers vs. Commanders liveDate: Monday, Oct. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: Levi's Stadium (Santa Clara, California)TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: 49ers -7.5, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Commanders have the ballJayden Daniels looked no worse for wear last week in his return from another dislocated elbow. He completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards, while also rushing nine times for 103 yards and two touchdowns. Had he and the entire offense not totally brain-farted at the end of overtime, it would have been a wildly encouraging performance for Washington's rest-of-season outlook.While Daniels has been excellent when taking off to run in his three starts, Washington's running backs have been extremely inefficient on the ground. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (who was ruled out for this game after not practicing all week), Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and the recently-released Kaytron Allen have combined to average just 3.7 yards per carry. The offensive line has created little push up front, with the backs collectively gaining just 0.95 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, and the backs themselves have broken tackles at the second-lowest rate in all of football.The 49ers, meanwhile, have allowed just 3.7 yards per rush to enemy running backs, with great tackling being the primary method of limiting yardage. Backs have gained 1.47 yards per carry before contact (an above-average mark), but only 2.22 yards after contact thanks to the lowest broken-tackle rate in the league. As a result, San Francisco has allowed only two explosive runs all season, per Tru Media, the fewest in the NFL.
San Francisco has also been mostly strong against the pass, checking in 10th in opponents' EPA per dropback and 5th in opponents' success rate. The 49ers have allowed quarterbacks to complete only 64.4% of their passes at an average of 6.1 yards per attempt, with just five touchdowns and three interceptions in five games.  It's tough to know what to make of Washington's passing game because it hasn't been at full strength for most of the season. Daniels missed two-and-a-half games. Chig Okonwko missed two. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs each missed one and saw their snaps limited in another. The Daniels-McLaurin-Diggs trio has shared the field for only 57 plays so far this season, according to Tru Media. Daniels is just 15 of 30 for 129 yards on those plays, but he has thrown for three scores and scrambled for 62 yards.Daniels should, in theory, see at least some clean pockets with the 49ers again playing without Nick Bosa, but Washington's offensive line has yielded pressure on over 38% of dropbacks so far this season, so the Niners could have a chance to get into Daniels' lap and force him into tough throws and mistakes. With the generally sticky coverage the San Francisco corners have played so far this season, it could be tough sledding for Washington in the passing game on Monday night.
When the 49ers have the ballSan Francisco has been the league's fourth-most efficient offense by EPA per play, according to Tru Media, ranking second with the pass and 14th with the run. Brock Purdy is playing at as high a level as any quarterback in football, completing 69% of his passes at an average of 8.4 yards per attempt with a league-high 13 touchdown passes and just two interceptions. Purdy also has a 57.9% passing success rate, which ranks as the best in the league.Purdy has done that despite hemorrhaging wide receivers throughout the season. Ricky Pearsall was lost for the year in training camp. Christian Kirk (listed as questionable for this week) has yet to make his 49er debut. De'Zhaun Stribling was injured in Week 1. Demarcus Robinson went down in Week 2. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing were knocked out of last week's win over the Seahawks. Mike Evans has been playing through a painful rib injury. (He's also questionable for Monday night.) George Kittle spent the first two weeks ramping up to a full workload after last season's Achilles tear. And yet, here the 49ers are. Washington, meanwhile, has been one of the league's friendliest pass defenses. Every team the Commanders have faced has thrown for at least 257 net yards. Four of the five teams have gone more than 300 and two of them exceeded 400. The Commanders have allowed opponents to complete 65.2% of passes at an average of 7.1 yards per attempt, with 14 touchdowns and just three interceptions. The 103.9 passer rating against the Commanders to date is the sixth-worst mark in the league. It's very easy to see San Francisco finding success through the air so long as Evans suits up for the game.
Christian McCaffrey is sharing the workload in the run game far more this season than in years past, with 61 carries for 286 yards againt Kaelon Black's 37 carries for 136 yards. McCaffrey's 4.7 yards-per-carry average is far better than what he posted over the last two years (4.0 and 3.9), and his rushing success rate of 45.9% is seventh-best out of 48 qualifying running backs. That figure is the second-best mark of his career, behind only the 2023 season, during which he led the NFL in rushing yards.The Commanders have actually been stingy against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry, with opposing backs limited to 0.69 yards per attempt before contact by the defensive front. Washington having similar success stopping the run here is important because it could make the 49ers one-dimensional, but the Commanders' pass-funnel defense also plays right into San Francisco's hands because of how efficient the 49ers' passing game has been so far this year. Purdy and Co. should eat, even if McCaffrey doesn't. PredictionI picked against the 49ers last week and regretted it almost immediately after seeing how their offense struggled against the stingy Seattle defense. Needless to say, Washington's defense is not of the same quality. I know the 49ers are still hemorrhaging wide receivers, but as long as Brock Purdy, Mike Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey are healthy and Kyle Shanahan is calling the plays, they are going to move the ball efficiently. And I don't trust the Commanders to do quite enough to keep up with their explosive offense.  Pick: 49ers 27, Commanders 16

title: Colts' fire GM Chris Ballard: What fire sale could look like if Indy trades DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson, others - CBS Sports
description: The Colts don't have a 2027 first-round pick. But what could they get for top veterans in preparation for a 2027
body:
The Colts don't have a 2027 first-round pick. But what could they get for top veterans in preparation for a 2027 rebuild?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Chris Ballard era as the Indianapolis Colts general manager came to an end on Monday. A 26-20 home loss against the previously 0-5 Tennessee Titans in Week 6 was enough for Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon to pull the plug on Ballard six games into his 10th season on the job.Under Ballard, Indianapolis reached the playoffs twice (2018 and 2020), going 1-2 in those two trips. The Colts' 72-82-1 regular season record under his management ranked 17th in the league during Ballard's tenure. Indianapolis's five missed playoffs in a row (since 2021) is the Colts' longest such streak since 1988 to 1994, and the team never won an AFC South title under Ballard.Now, the franchise is left to pick up the pieces with a 2027 rebuild on the horizon. The good news is that the 2027 NFL Draft is widely regarded as one of the most talented in years. The bad news is that the Colts don't have a first-round pick thanks to trading their 2026 and 2027 first-round draft choices, as well as wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, to the New York Jets in exchange for All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner last season.However, there are multiple ways for Indianapolis to recoup draft capital through veterans on tradable deals. Let's take a look at what a potential fire sale of three of the Colts' top players could look like. 
DT DeForest Buckner
Three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner all but demanded a trade after the team's Week 6 loss against the Tennessee Titans. "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Buckner told reporters postgame on Sunday.   At 32 years old, Buckner still has plenty of gas in the tank. His 4.0 sacks through six weeks are tied for the 10th most in the NFL, while his 19 quarterback pressures rank as the seventh most among defensive tackles in 2026. The Colts would be unwise not to make him available, as he is set to become a free agent in the 2027 offseason. What could his market look like?
For a player at his age and contract status, this could be one of his last prime seasons, but for legitimate contenders, that could be worth a third-or fourth-round pick. Teams who could be interested could include the Green Bay Packers (4-2), the San Francisco 49ers (5-0) and the Minnesota Vikings (5-0). The Packers lost defensive tackle Javon Hargrave for the season with a torn Achilles, so it would make sense for them to place a call for Buckner. The 49ers make too much sense. That's where Buckner played his first four seasons, culminating in the 49ers losing Super Bowl LIV to the Kansas City Chiefs to conclude the 2019 season. He was traded to the Colts for a first-round pick in the 2020 offseason. San Francisco is going through its regularly scheduled injury catastrophe, which has hit their defensive line hard. If the Vikings want a mentor for rookie first-round pick Caleb Banks and another high-level contributor for defensive coordinator Brian Flores to get creative with, they would make sense as a win-now team. LG Quenton Nelson
Colts left guard Quenton Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler and a three-time first-team All-Pro, is primed to be one of the NFL's most coveted free agents next offseason ahead of his 31st birthday on March 19. This season, Nelson is currently Pro Football Focus' highest-graded guard in the entire NFL with an 89.2 offensive grade. 
He is a big fish who could net the Colts a second-round pick or perhaps a first-round choice if the bidding for his services gets frisky at the trade deadline. The complication is that he would be a rental or someone who would demand a top-of-the-market extension for whoever trades for his services. Who could line up for him? The Packers, a team that has been playing mix-and-match with an injury-plagued front, have stabilized their offensive line with the same starting five combination. But they could be in the mix, since they're currently rolling with aging veterans they signed off the street to start for them. If the Houston Texans (2-4), winners of two in a row, continue to climb, perhaps they would be interested. However, their asking price could be higher since they're a fellow AFC South team. The Vikings could be interested if they want to upgrade for undrafted free agent Joe Huber at left guard, with Donovan Jackson out with a torn meniscus. The 49ers, who are currently starting 2025 seventh-round pick Connor Colby at left guard, could make an all-in trade for Nelson. 
RB Jonathan Taylor 
The Colts don't need to trade three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor. He is still just 27 years old, and he re-signed with Indianapolis on a two-year extension worth $44 million with $39 million in total guarantees in August. However, if the Colts want to jumpstart their rebuild in earnest, parting with Taylor now could perhaps net them a first-round pick. They could point toward the impact top-end running backs Kenneth Walker III, Bijan Robinson, Jahmyr Gibbs and others are having all around the league as reason to demand a 2027 or a 2028 first-round pick in return.Indianapolis could perhaps engage two AFC North teams, the Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) and the Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2), in a bidding war. The Bengals are averaging the fifth-fewest rushing yards per game (82.8) in the entire league this season, while Aaron Rodgers could use more support for the Steelers' 13th-worst running game (99.2 rushing yards per game) in what appears to be his NFL swan song. The Packers trading a 2028 first and another pick or two for Taylor could give them the runway to release Josh Jacobs after some legal trouble landed him on the commissioner's exempt list for the first six weeks of the 2026 season. They rank dead last in the league in rushing (59.8 rushing yards per game), and Taylor is a former Wisconsin Badger. Trading for him would earn them public relations bonus points by dumping Jacobs and bringing a local product home.
